name: Schematic
reference: IBM's Carbon design system in its darkest theme: grey 100, IBM Plex, hairline diagrams with labels.
pattern: Grey-black ground, white and grey type, one IBM blue for the active path.
personality: Engineering. Systems drawn in white hairlines, labelled and measured.

accentElements.note: One accent element in a frame: the active path (its lines and the labels that sit on it read as one part). The rest of the drawing is in ink.

motion.character: Productive: lines draw, labels follow, the active path lights in blue.
motion.transitions: The camera pans along the diagram to the next part.

texture.note: A hairline grid. Never a blue blueprint tint.

grammar: Diagrams in white hairlines with mono labels.
The blue marks only the active path or the part being explained.
Dimension lines and callout numbers, as in a schematic.

pictures.note: A reference photo in a measured window, quiet grey; the drawing is the hero.

hits.note: A dry tick as a dimension or label locks.

compose.how: The question in a status line at the text-safe top. The figure box under it spans the picture-safe width down to 86 % of the frame's height (`figureBox`); fitDrawing with no area stands the drawing on that foot, across the text column, so the drawing fills the lower band with picture (only picture may go there; the last 14 % stays clear). Its labels and dimensions take the text-safe area: make one `figure` of the drawing's parts (with `pulley` and `rope` for wheels and ropes) and give it to each `dimension` and `callout`, and they place themselves clear of every stroke, of the status line and of each other (a force's name at its arrow's tail, dimensions just clear of what they span, a chain on one line). A dimension of a part in the lower band keeps its lines there and puts its value on a short leader in the text-safe area. Name a part by a point near the text-safe area (the top of a load in the lower band, not its foot). Lay a plate under it with the sheet's `plate`: the plate is the figure box, and the figure with its labels fills it from its foot up. Stand the parts with `boxAt` and `pointOf` (a fulcrum's apex under a beam), and rest one part on another with shape `on`, never with hand-computed moves. An equation or a note goes in the status line, or in a box from the figure's `place`. The hook counts the plate with its drawing as one picture; the empty-frame check counts only the drawing's lines, labels and dimensions as content, never the grid or the empty part of a plate.

hook.how: The full diagram in hairlines on frame 0, with the question in a status line above it.

moves.move: Lines draw, labels follow, and the active path lights in blue.

measurable.how: The accent covers one connected region per key frame: the active path.

moves.move: The camera pans along the diagram; a status line stays on screen through every pan.

measurable.how: A sentence stays on screen through every pan.

moves.move: The answer is drawn: dimension lines and callout numbers, not only typed.
A hairline grid under the diagram.

measurable.how: Hairlines at a fixed pitch in every key frame.

props.kind: "rect" for a beam or a load, "triangle" for a fulcrum (its points from pointOf: "apex", "base")
props.on: the part it rests on and the point: { part: fulcrum, at: "apex" }; it rides and turns with that part
props.pivot: the point it turns about (default: the point it rests on)

blocks.for: The parts of a mechanism that rest on each other and turn, with no hand-computed move.

props.figure: the drawing's figure: the dimension takes the nearest clear tier, and its value goes on its line or on a short leader in the text-safe area
props.side: "above" (default), "left" or "right" for a height; the error names a side that works
props.follow: the part's keys when it moves

blocks.for: Dimension lines in tiers outside the drawing, measured square to the side they stand on.

props.label: the part's name or its force, short (a label beside a 9:16 drawing has about 4 words of room)
props.number: the callout number, where the label is short enough
props.target: a point on the part, near the text-safe area
props.figure: the drawing's figure: the label goes next to its target, clear of every stroke, label and leader

blocks.for: Callouts whose short leaders end on the part.

props.run: the stops: the fixed end, each wheel (a `pulley`: r from fitDrawing, `moves` for a wheel that rises, `turns` from rollDegrees) with its turn, the free end (with `follow` when it moves)
props.light: the active path, in the accent

blocks.for: An open rope over pulleys (wheels with no teeth that turn by key marks) whose strands change length as a wheel moves.

props.role: "headline" for the question (the hook's role); "label" for the status line's small print

blocks.for: The question and the status line, pinned, so they ride through the `camera` pans along the diagram (camera `moves`).

props.plate: true: the plate under the drawing, the figure box

blocks.for: The complete hairline grid, the plate and the title block; fitDrawing stands the drawing in figureBox.

props.r: from fitDrawing, or heroBox: the drawing covers the hook's share of the frame
props.color: "accent" on the driving gear (the active part), the rest in ink

blocks.for: Sprockets on one tooth pitch, turning at the true ratio; `belt` draws the chain on their outer tangents, the active path in blue.

avoid.why: Pictures are rare; the drawing explains.

ends.how: A full elevation at a scale where everything fits, with the answer's dimension drawn last (its lines in the lower band where the part stands there, its value in the text-safe area) on one of the loudest bars (`beats().loudest`).
ends.with: the answer's dimension drawn last on one of the loudest bars, its tick from `hit({ on })`, then `hold` to the end (the closing hold is exempt from the stillness rule)

mix.note: Steady techno. Enter on a section whose bars are among the track's loudest (`beats().loudest` for the film's window is not empty), so the answer can land on one. A dry tick as each dimension locks, 6 dB over the bed.

shots.match: One drawing at one scale, or the scale break labelled.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
